find:
For two resistors in parallel, use the formula: 1 ÷ Rtotal = 1 ÷ R1 + 1 ÷ R2

Example: Two resistors of 6 Ω and 12 Ω are connected in parallel. Find the total resistance.

1 ÷ Rtotal = 1 ÷ 6 + 1 ÷ 12 = 2 ÷ 12 + 1 ÷ 12 = 3 ÷ 12

Rtotal = 12 ÷ 3 = \(4 \, \Omega\)

Notice that 4 Ω is less than the smallest individual resistor (6 Ω). This is always the case with parallel resistors.

expect: A student connects three identical lamps in parallel to a 12 V battery. Each lamp has a resistance of 6 Ω. Calculate the total resistance of the three lamps. Explain what would happen to the brightness of the remaining lamps if one lamp were removed from the circuit.
value: A student connects three identical lamps in parallel to a 12 V battery. Each lamp has a resistance of 6 Ω. Compare the potential difference across each lamp and the current in each lamp with the same three lamps connected in series. Explain what happens to the total resistance of the circuit and to the brightness of the lamps when a fourth identical lamp is added in parallel.
note: F3: the 6-mark question asked for a total parallel resistance calculation. Rewritten on the same circuit as a qualitative comparison of current, potential difference, the effect of adding a lamp and brightness.

expect:
Indicative content (6 marks):
• 1/Rₜₒₜₐₗ = 1/6 + 1/6 + 1/6 = 3/6 (1)
• Rₜₒₜₐₗ = 6/3 = 2 Ω (1)
• In a parallel circuit, voltage across each branch is the same / 12 V (1)
• Removing one lamp does not change the voltage across the remaining lamps (1)
• The current through each remaining lamp stays the same (I = V/R = 12/6 = 2 A) (1)
• Therefore the brightness of the remaining lamps does not change (1)

Allow: credit for stating that total resistance of the circuit increases when a branch is removed, and total current from the battery decreases.
value:
Indicative content (6 marks):
• In parallel, each lamp has the full 12 V across it (1)
• In series, the 12 V is shared, so each lamp has only 4 V across it (1)
• The current in each lamp is larger in parallel, so the lamps are brighter in parallel (1)
• Adding a fourth lamp in parallel gives the current another path, so the total resistance falls (1)
• The total current drawn from the battery increases (1)
• Each lamp still has the full 12 V across it, so the brightness of the other lamps does not change (1)

Allow: the total resistance of the parallel circuit is always less than the resistance of one lamp. Accept “each lamp is brighter in parallel than in series” for the third mark.
